title: Fraud alert queue, June to September 2026

findings.headline: Nine in ten alerts are false positives
findings.detail: Only 313 of 3,000 alerts (10.4%) were confirmed fraud, so about 2,687 alerts produced no fraud. Analyst time is going on alerts that rarely pay off.

findings.headline: Three rules carry most of the confirmed fraud
findings.detail: Mule account inbound (31.7%), New device + high amount (21.9%) and Velocity (15.4%) have the highest hit rates. Round-amount transfer (0.6%) and Night-time login (1.6%) together make up 33.3% of alerts and rarely find fraud.

findings.headline: New device rule hit rate rising month on month
findings.detail: Its confirmed-fraud rate went from 18.1% in June to 24.3% in September. This is the largest alerts-volume rule among the high-yield ones (556 alerts), so it is worth understanding why.

findings.headline: Larger amounts and longer handling go with fraud
findings.detail: The top fifth of amounts (£34,533 and above, if in pounds) has a 19.8% fraud rate against 3.7% for the lowest fifth. Alerts taking over 15 minutes to handle are 33.3% fraud, against 0.7% for 7 minutes or less.

findings.headline: Volumes steady and data is clean
findings.detail: Monthly alerts ranged from 694 to 793 and the fraud rate from 9.7% to 11.1%, with no missing cells or duplicates. Analyst fraud rates range from 6.0% to 13.1%, but the mix of alerts each analyst receives is unknown.

next_steps: Review whether Round-amount transfer and Night-time login rules can be tightened or down-prioritised, checking first that no confirmed fraud would be lost.
Investigate why New device + high amount hit rates rose from 18.1% to 24.3%, and check whether alert thresholds or fraud patterns changed.
Check whether analyst differences, such as Analyst 06 at 6.0% versus Analyst 05 at 13.1%, reflect different rule mixes before drawing conclusions.

conclusion: The queue is clean and stable, but about nine in ten alerts are false positives, and most real fraud comes from three rules: Mule account inbound, New device + high amount and Velocity. Two rules, Round-amount transfer and Night-time login, make up a third of alerts and found very little fraud. Start by reviewing those two low-yield rules, while checking nothing important would be lost.
limits: This review uses summary statistics only, so it cannot show why rules differ, whether fraud was missed, or whether analyst differences reflect skill or the alerts they were given.
